concept: A large owl whose entire face is a total eclipse — a perfect black disc ringed by a thin corona of pale silver. It embodies the moment dawn fails: the light blocked, the ring remaining. Moves in absolute silence; its wing beats displace no air.
visual: Large swooping owl, ink-black plumage with silver edge-highlights; a total-eclipse disc face (black with silver corona ring); talons that phase in and out of visibility; wingspan fills a two-tile span.
signature_idea: Total Eclipse — Dark/Lunar move; negates all stat boosts on the opponent's side for 3 turns as the 'eclipse' blots them out
hook: A face that IS an eclipse — silhouette unlike any other kin in the dex.

name: Basilk
concept: A low-slung lizard of basalt-black stone whose underbelly glows with a very faint void-light — not because it produces light but because the null within it has a dim sheen. It petrifies small creatures with its gaze.
visual: Flat-bodied lizard, rough basalt-textured hide of dark grey-black; faint purple underlight glow at belly; stony crest ridge along spine; eyes are not pupils but smooth obsidian spheres.
hook: A stone-lizard with void in its belly — the glow is wrong, not warm, and kids will clock the wrongness instantly.

name: Nullserpent
concept: A massive coiling serpent of black basalt, its body segmented like stacked columns of volcanic rock. Each segment is edged with dim void-light. Where it passes, the ground goes cold and dark, and crystal formations of null-stone grow in its wake.
visual: Long coiling snake, body composed of stacked basalt drum-segments with dark-violet rims; head is a flat ritual-mask shape of polished obsidian; null-crystal spines along upper edges; heavy, geological presence.
signature_idea: Basalt Null — physical Stone/Dark combo move; leaves Null-stone field that lowers Light-type move power
hook: A geological serpent — a snake that is literally a geological event.

name: Huskling
concept: A small hollow-bird — a finch-like kin whose song has been drained to a faint whisper. It perches on snuffed lanterns in the coldfog, repeating a soft, toneless refrain of a song it no longer remembers.
visual: Compact small-bird form, ashen dove-grey, beak slightly open as if mid-song; chest slightly caved-in suggesting hollowness; wings dusted in null-grey; feet clutch an invisible perch; simple but sad silhouette.
hook: The bird that can't remember its own song — a simple, devastating image.

name: Voidchoir
concept: A large corvid-like hollow-bird that has forgotten every melody — instead its call is a resonant null-tone that scrambles opponents' senses. It gathers flocks of smaller hollow kin around it as if trying to reconstruct a chorus.
visual: Large raven-silhouette, void-black plumage with subtle shifting void-iridescence (not sparkle but depth); beak wide and edged in dull bone; one eye dim-white, one completely dark; tail fan like a spread hand of dead feathers.
signature_idea: Null Choir — status move; inflicts Confuse + Dim on target; only useable while another Dark-type is in the party (flavour: the missing chorus)
hook: A bird trying to sing back what it lost — gathers hollow kin like it's assembling a choir.

name: Siltgloom
concept: A bell-shaped void-jellyfish that drifts through the coldfog marshes like its ocean-going cousins drift through water. Its translucent body contains a dark core that pulses slowly — not light, but the absence of it.
visual: Wide bell-jellyfish silhouette, nearly transparent grey-white body with a central void-dark core pulsing slowly; long trailing tendrils of shadow-mist rather than filaments; reads as a floating bell at 24px.
signature_idea: Null Bell — passive ability; on taking a special hit, reflects 1/4 of the damage back as Dark-type
hook: A jellyfish of fog rather than water — the void core that pulses where bioluminescence should be.

name: Driftmare
concept: A spectral horse-kin that gallops through the coldfog without touching ground. Its mane trails void-smoke; its hooves leave dark imprints that fade after three steps. Once a proud creature, now carrying a rider it can no longer remember.
visual: Lean equine form, ashen bone-white with void-dark mane and tail that flow upward regardless of direction; translucent lower legs fading to mist at the hooves; a hollow saddle-shaped depression on its back; galloping pose as default.
signature_idea: Phantom Gallop — priority-speed move, Dark-type; user gains +1 Speed after use
hook: A ghost-horse with an empty saddle — invites every player to imagine the missing rider.

name: Crestfall
concept: A hollow-bird heron that once guided marsh-travelers with a bioluminescent crest — but its crest has collapsed into trailing null-feathers. It stands at the edge of stagnant pools and watches the dark surface for a reflection that never comes.
visual: Tall elegant heron stance, slate-grey feathers, a long drooping crest of charcoal null-feathers where a bright plume once stood; neck curved in a melancholy bow; mirror-finish eyes reflecting nothing; single-tile tall at rest.
signature_idea: Mourning Dive — strong physical Dark move with recoil; recoil is halved if the user is below half HP
hook: A once-beautiful guide-heron whose crest has fallen — standing at the water watching for a reflection.

name: Bogvast
concept: An enormous null-beast that has become part of the coldfog marshes themselves — its body encrusted with dead reed-stalks, snuffed lantern-frames, and darkened mineral deposits. Travelers have always assumed it was a piece of geography. It moves only when something enters its null-field.
visual: Vast tortoise-like creature, entirely hidden beneath an shell of snuffed lanterns, dead reeds, and null-stone; only the deep void-dark eyes and four pillar-legs betray it as alive; its back looks like a section of blighted marsh terrain.
signature_idea: Stillmarch — on entry, sets a terrain field that reduces all opponents' Speed by one stage per turn spent in battle; the 'being slowly swallowed by the marsh' feeling
hook: An apex creature that IS the coldfog marsh — players who didn't look carefully will be stunned when it moves.

name: Lamplit
concept: A small four-legged kin with a lantern growing from its forehead — but the lantern-cage on its brow is dark, the glass cracked and the interior null-black. It trots ahead of travelers like a guide-dog, though the light it offers is none at all.
visual: Compact dog-form, muted teal-grey coat, a small iron lantern-cage mounted on its brow pointing forward; the lantern is visibly dead (cracked glass, blackened interior); tail held up like a guide beacon that isn't working.
hook: A guide-dog with a broken lantern — it still tries to lead you, and that makes it precious.

name: Dimward
concept: A large hound whose lantern-head has grown into a full iron lantern-helm — the cage is elaborate now, elegant ironwork. The lantern remains dark. In battle, it uses the null inside the lantern as a weapon, venting void-pressure at opponents.
visual: Large hound form, deep slate coat, an ornate iron lantern-cage helm on its head that frames its face; the lantern-glass panes are void-black; null-vapour seeps from the lantern vents; decorative chain leash fused to its collar.
signature_idea: Null Vent — releases pressurised void from the lantern; lowers opponent Speed and SpDef simultaneously; must be recharged (1-turn wait) like a real fuel cycle
hook: The beautiful irony of an exquisite lantern-helm that gives no light — form without function, made formidable.

name: Vaporetch
concept: A will-o'-wisp-descended marsh-sprite whose inner flame has been replaced by compressed null-vapour — a mote of darkness rather than light. It hovers erratically and can burn with cold dark rather than heat.
visual: Teardrop wisp-sprite, glassy outer shell showing the null-vapour core within (dark violet-black, slowly swirling); trails of cold null-mist; a faint crack along its surface leaking void; small but ominous.
hook: A wisp where the fire went out and something else moved in — the wrong kind of glow.

name: Dreadlume
concept: A large dark-luminous being shaped like a lantern-ghost — a tall pillar of void with a lantern housing visible within it, now the lantern of a Hollowing-light. It illuminates nothing but itself, casting an anti-shadow that darkens what should be bright.
visual: Tall upright lantern-ghost form, body is a pillar of near-opaque void-smoke with a visible internal lantern structure lit by anti-light (dark illumination — the surrounding area visibly dims near it); arms are dissolving void-tendrils.
signature_idea: Anti-Illuminate — reduces all Light-type damage done to the user to 0.5×; once per battle, converts one incoming Light move's damage into HP
hook: A lantern-ghost that runs on anti-light — everything near it dims, including hope.

name: Ashwing
concept: A small shadow-bat whose echolocation emits void-frequencies instead of sound — it maps the world in dark silence. The wings are charred-looking, as if burnt out by something too cold rather than too hot.
visual: Small bat form, charred-ash wings with thin void-membrane stretched between; body compact and sooty-dark; ears large and dish-shaped for null-frequency sensing; hangs at rest rather than perches, upside-down.
hook: A bat that echolocates with void — it can map the dark no one else can navigate.

name: Voidwing
concept: A large null-ray, bat-like and flat — it cruises the coldfog at height, its vast wing-membrane a sheet of concentrated shadow. Where it passes, the coldfog thickens briefly, as if it exhales the Hollowing itself.
visual: Wide flat ray-like bat, enormous wing-membrane of deep void-black that shifts with a slow ripple like disturbed water; tiny head, wide flat body, long whip-tail; underside a paler matte grey; massive presence at full sprite.
signature_idea: Fogbreath — creates a null-fog field for 5 turns; reduces accuracy of all non-Dark moves by 20%
hook: A shadow-manta-ray that cruises above the marshes — a flat shape that fills the sky is instantly fearsome.

name: Tombcrawl
concept: A heavy crustacean-like husk-crab that carries pieces of dead architecture on its back — snuffed lamp-glass, broken lantern frames, iron fittings from the Hollowfen Stillworks. It scavenges the remains of what once gave light.
visual: Wide low crab-body, charcoal chitinous shell; its broad back is visibly cluttered with salvage — cracked lamp-glass, a bent iron lantern-frame; claws are oversized and asymmetric; moves slowly but implacably.
signature_idea: Salvage Shell — passive; taking physical damage has a 30% chance to drop a held item onto the field as a temporary barrier
hook: A husk-crab wearing the ruins of civilisation on its back — a moving museum of the Hollowing.

name: Penumbreed
concept: A tiny reed-creature — a husk larva that has grown inside a hollow reed-stalk in the blighted marsh. Its translucent carapace shows a dim void-core; it clings to the inside of dead vegetation.
visual: Small tube-bodied larva form, pale milky-white outer casing (like a reed section), with a dark void-core visible within; vestigial limb-stubs; minimal face — two flat dark eye-discs; horizontal rest pose.
hook: A thing living inside the dead reeds — the marsh has become its home and husk alike.

name: Voidreed
concept: A tall, slender null-construct that has grown out of its reed-stalk housing — now upright, shaped vaguely humanoid, its body a column of woven dead reeds with a void-core running top to bottom. It is more constructed-looking than born.
visual: Tall thin reed-woven humanoid, dark hollow at chest and head; woven reed texture with void showing through the gaps; arms are bundles of hollow stems that droop; crown is a ring of broken reeds like a snuffed wreath.
hook: A kin that looks made rather than born — woven from the dead material of the marsh.

name: Marshwarden
concept: The final form of the reed-larva: a woven colossus that has absorbed decades of null-growth, standing tall as a doorway, armored in compressed dead-reed and null-crystal. It cannot speak but it stations itself — it guards the entrance to places the Hollowing claims.
visual: Large upright woven-reed golem, deep charcoal reed-weave over a visible void-crystal skeleton; shoulders broad and reinforced with iron-dark bracings; a halo of bent dead reeds frames the featureless void-face; deeply imposing.
signature_idea: Null Warden — passive ability; takes 0.75× from all special moves; allies behind it take 0.5× from special moves for one turn per switch
hook: A golem woven from the marsh's own grief — a warden of a place that no longer needs guarding, but does it anyway.

name: Cindervast
concept: The Drownlight Beacon sub-legendary — a vast shadow-whale that was once a Solar-type celestial guardian of the old beacon. The Hollowing snuffed its stored daylight entirely and refashioned it into a creature of pure null. It circles the beacon's foundations in the deep fog, singing a song at a frequency no living thing can hear.
visual: Enormous cetacean silhouette, deep void-black with faint silver constellation-marks still visible along its flanks (the ghost of what it was); fins trail null-mist; a crescent of anti-light glows where its blowhole was; awe-tier size.
signature_idea: Null Tide — the signature: a wave of void that hits the entire opposing side; drains one positive stat stage from each target; requires the Drownlight Beacon encounter to access
hook: A beacon-whale who once lit the coast, now the dark that extinguishes it — the most poignant creature in the dex.

name: Pyrevast
concept: The luminous anchor of the Ember Constellation, a great bull-like creature whose entire body is a walking forge of slow, eternal flame. Vesperholm legend calls it the Hearthwarden — the one who first lit the south valley's lanterns at the dawn of time. Its hide is layered ash-iron, and between each plate glows a steady amber-to-white heat, like embers in a temple hearth. When it stands still, its breath rises as soft smoke-rings that cool into constellation shapes. Caught only in the depths of the Tinderwick Lumenary's secret shrine after the Ember constellation is relit.
visual: Massive bull-deer silhouette with broad-swept antlers; each antler tip burns as an open flame. Body plating is charcoal-grey with deep amber veins of living heat between the plates. A mane of slow, diamond-cyan-accented embers trails behind the neck. Eyes are molten white-gold. Reads as an immovable, cathedral-warm presence at any sprite size.
signature_idea: Hearthmount — the user roots to the ground, raising its own Special Defense dramatically and dealing reflected Special damage back at any attacker for two turns; a slow, immovable counter-blow that feels like a furnace wall.
hook: The impossible: a fire-type that tanks. A kid who finds this in the shrine will feel like they've discovered a secret the game doesn't advertise.

name: Tidesovran
concept: The luminous anchor of the Tide Constellation, a colossal manta-like creature that drifts through Pearlmoor Quay's deepest sea-shrine when the moon is full. It is said to have been born from the first tide that ever pulled back from shore, taking memory of the dry world with it into the deep. Its wing-fins are translucent as sea-glass, filled with slow-spinning bioluminescent currents. The pearl at the centre of its brow is the 'locked' drop of the Tide star — when it is found, the Tide Constellation glimmers even on cloudy nights.
visual: Enormous manta silhouette, wing-span exceeding its body length; the disc-body glows from within with tidal blue and pearl-white, veined with diamond-cyan light currents. The brow bears a single luminous pearl like a dropped moon. Trailing 'star-wake' tail fins fan into constellation-dot patterns. Against the night-sea palette it reads as a slow, otherworldly sail.
signature_idea: Moonpull — a surging Special strike that deals tide-type damage and always lowers the target's Special Defense by one stage; the tidal force that carries everything with it.
hook: A sea-manta made of moonlight and memory — the sight of it emerging from the shrine's dark water will be the defining screenshot of many playthroughs.

name: Verdanthral
concept: The luminous anchor of the Verdant Constellation, a slow ancient tortoise whose shell has grown into a living canopy of bioluminescent ferns, capped with a single enormous glowmoss-lantern tree. Its shell is a micro-ecosystem; fireflies and tiny Verdant kin shelter inside its leaf-arches. Lowleaf Hollow's deepest grove-shrine holds it asleep; it wakes only when someone brings the full glow of a restored Verdant star back to the hollow. Its footsteps leave behind glowing spore-prints that linger for hours.
visual: Massive tortoise with a domed shell entirely overgrown with tall diamond-cyan glowing ferns and a central mossy tree trunk sprouting upward. Legs are bark-textured, slow-pillar limbs. Eyes glow a deep verdant green. The silhouette at any scale reads as a walking forest — a living habitat, not just a creature.
signature_idea: Canopy Ward — summons a living light-canopy that blocks all non-contact moves for two turns and heals the user slightly each turn; a patience-rewarding fortress move.
hook: A tortoise that is also a forest. Kids who love the idea of having a whole ecosystem on their side will treasure this.

name: Gravenmere
concept: The luminous anchor of the Stone Constellation, a towering ram-golem formed from the deepest veins of Cinderhead Mine — part living crystal, part animate bedrock. The Stone star is mapped to the ore-heart of Vesperholm's deepest earth; this creature is the ground's memory of light. Its horns are twin columns of faceted diamond-lit quartz that refract the Mine's lantern-fire into a full spectrum. When struck, shards of it break away and hover, orbiting its body like a slow-spinning asteroid field.
visual: Bipedal ram-golem, stocky and vast; body is layered dark stone with veins of diamond-cyan crystal running through every surface. Massive sweeping horns, each faceted and emitting cool spectra of light. Floating stone-shard orbits the shoulders. Face is blunt, ancient, carved — like a relief from a mine wall made animate.
signature_idea: Geode Shatter — a physical strike so powerful it sends orbiting crystal shards flying into the target, dealing physical Stone damage and trapping the target in a mineral prison that reduces Speed for three turns.
hook: A mountain that fights back. The floating-shard orbit is a visual designers will love rendering in the battle screen.

name: Squallmajor
concept: The luminous anchor of the Storm Constellation, a vast raptor-eagle whose wingspan encompasses a personal storm front. Galehigh Terraces' sky-shrine sits atop the highest terrace, reachable only by Updraft Kite; this creature inhabits the eye of the permanent column of cloud above it. It is said to have been the first being to understand the difference between lightning and light — that the sky's violence and the sky's beauty share a source. Its feathers are alternating obsidian and diamond-cyan crackling arc-light.
visual: Great eagle shape, enormous — wing-span dwarfs the battle frame. Feathers are obsidian-dark edged with crackling cyan electric arcs. The breast has a constellation-map burn pattern in gold-white. Eyes are storm-grey with a lightning-flash pupil. Each wing-beat displaces a visible shockwave ring.
signature_idea: Skyweave Strike — dives from above in a massive physical arc-lightning blow; deals dual physical and special damage (split evenly) and creates a two-turn lightning field that boosts Storm-type move power for both sides.
hook: The one legendary-tier encounter where the arena literally shakes. Players who catch it will brag about it.

name: Icelantern
concept: The luminous anchor of the Frost Constellation, a great elk-like creature whose antlers have grown into elaborate frozen chandeliers of pale blue ice, each tip ending in a hovering aurora-mote. Pale Vault Glacier's hidden ice-cathedral holds it in a deep freeze, waiting. Ysolde Frost says it speaks in riddles because it remembers every winter and the answers are all the same one. Its body is pale as new snow, but its core glows with the frozen light of the aurora it carries within itself — a star that chose to be cold.
visual: Tall, slender elk; coat is white-silver with a faint aurora-shimmer. Antlers branch into chandelier formations of fused ice-crystal, each tip emitting a small hovering aurora-mote in green and diamond-cyan. The underbelly glows a steady pale blue. Breath mists into aurora-ribbon shapes. The silhouette reads as regal, lonely, vast.
signature_idea: Aurora Veil — casts a shimmering aurora screen that halves all incoming Special damage for three turns and causes any attacker to become confused by the light-play.
hook: The aurora elk is one of those images that transcends the game: stark, beautiful, and melancholy in exactly the Vesperholm way.

name: Solarmourn
concept: The luminous anchor of the Solar Constellation, a great heron-phoenix whose plumage is the last fragment of stored daylight in the Sunken Solarium. It doesn't burn — it glows with the warm memory of sunlight, a diffuse gold that makes everything it stands beside look briefly like afternoon. Lucan Pyre found it roosting in the solarium's highest dry arch, a decade ago, and has kept its presence secret, because he was afraid. It embodies not the heat of the sun but the feeling of warmth remembered — a comfort, not a weapon.
visual: Tall, elegant heron-phoenix with long sweeping tail feathers that trail behind like a train. Plumage in warm gold and honey-amber, edged with faint diamond-cyan light. The chest and neck are pale as bone-white parchment. One wing is slightly shorter — an old wound that never quite healed. Eyes are deep amber, warm and patient. The silhouette is all grace and faded glory.
signature_idea: Last Warm Day — floods the battlefield with stored solar warmth, raising all allies' Speed and Special Attack for three turns while giving the user near-perfect priority on its next move; a pivot move built from memory.
hook: The sorrowful beauty of something magnificent that has endured too long alone. Players who battle this one in the Solarium will feel the whole Vesperholm mood in one encounter.

name: Lunaveil
concept: The luminous anchor of the Lunar Constellation, a silken serpent-moth of impossible size — its wingspan covers the Nightreach Observatory's dome when it alights. Nessa Cole has been tracking its orbital path through the sky for years without knowing what it was. It navigates by the Lunar star alone; when that star was dimmed, it circled the Observatory for months, lost, and finally settled behind the great lens. Its wings are the night sky itself, each scale a pinprick of cold blue starlight. When it moves, it leaves a fading trail of lunar dust.
visual: Vast serpent-body with two enormous moth-wings, each wing a deep night-blue scattered with hundreds of cold diamond-cyan star-point scales. The serpent body is dark as ink with a faint silver-blue iridescence. The head is moth-like with long feeler-antennae tipped with cold silver sparks. In the night-blue palette of the Observatory, it is nearly invisible until it moves.
signature_idea: Lunar Drift — phases partially out of material existence, making the user immune to all moves for one turn and then slamming back into reality with a high-Speed special strike that always moves first.
hook: The night sky as a creature. Anyone who watches its entrance animation will screenshot it immediately.

name: Keylumen
concept: The Keystar-kin. At the heart of the Umbral Spire, sealed within the Ninth Lantern, rests the being that the old Vesperholm star-tenders simply called the First Light — the original anchor of the Keystar, the central star without which no other constellation can hold. Keylumen is not a creature that chose to be a star: it is a star that chose to become a creature, once, long ago, because it was curious about the world below. It is vast and tender and utterly singular. When the Hollowing's Great Null reaches toward the Keystar, Keylumen rises from within the darkened lantern — not to fight, but to remember. And in remembering, it outshines everything around it. Scripted encounter; cannot be encountered in the wild.
visual: A tall, upright cervine figure — like a great stag, but made entirely of woven starlight. No hard edges: the silhouette blooms and shifts like a constellation drawing. The body is a deep midnight-blue field shot through with dense white-gold star-points; the antlers are open latticework of pure light, each tip a true star. The eyes are two full-disc pupils of warm solar gold. At rest it looks like a lantern-constellation stepped down from the sky. In battle it pulses with ever-brightening rings of diamond-cyan. The art reads iconic at every sprite size.
signature_idea: Keylight — the Keystar flares through the user, striking all opposing kin simultaneously with pure Light damage that ignores resistances and then leaving a Radiance field that heals the user's side each turn for three turns; the move that relights the sky.
hook: Keylumen is the answer to the whole game's question. Catching it feels not like a victory but like being trusted.

name: Nullmajor
concept: Warden Còr's drained final-boss kin — the embodiment of the Great Null, the shape that all the harvested light takes when there is nowhere left to go. Nullmajor is not malicious. It is vast and sorrowful, the accumulated darkness of every snuffed lantern and every constellation dimmed by the Hollowing's null-lanterns. In battle at the Umbral Spire's peak, it does not attack: it absorbs. It pulls light from the air, from the player's kin, from the Skyweave Crown itself. To face it is to understand what Còr was trying to create — a world where the pain of losing light simply stops, because there is none left. Post-story, Còr releases it; it dissolves into the sky as dawn returns, becoming the last dark before morning.
visual: A colossal figure, roughly humanoid in silhouette — but hollow. The outline is a dense ink-black void rimmed with a faint cold-violet corona. Within the outline is not darkness but anti-light: a negative space where the battle background is inverted, as if the creature is a hole in the world. Còr's null-lantern floats at the centre of its chest, still lit with inverted cold-violet. The face is a smooth featureless oval of pure absence. No eyes. It is the saddest design in the game — it looks like grief given form.
signature_idea: Great Null — draws every Light-typed bonus, Radiance effect, and STAB boost from the field into itself, converting them to raw Dark power and unleashing them as a single devastating pulse that also lowers all enemy kin's Special Attack for two turns; the anti-dawn.
hook: The final boss that makes players feel the weight of the story's moral. Not hateable — heartbreaking. The memory of this fight is the one that lasts.

name: Dawnbrael
concept: The Dawn Legendary — the kin that was always there, sleeping beneath Dawnstead in a sealed reliquary of sunrise-stone, waiting for the day that never came. It is not a new creature: it is the oldest kin in Vesperholm, the guardian of the first dawn, placed there by the original star-tenders as a failsafe for a worst case they hoped would never arrive. When dawn finally returns and the Dawnstead reliquary opens, Dawnbrael emerges as a lion-stag blazing with actual sunlight — not stored, not remembered, but real. For the first time in the game, a kin casts hard-edged shadows behind it. It is the payoff for finishing everything.
visual: A lion-stag — lion's body with a stag's great antlers — made of and wreathed in actual sunlight. The coat is amber-to-white radiance, the mane a full halo of solar corona arcs in diamond-cyan and fire-orange. The antlers are molten gold with sun-flare tips, casting hard shadows in every direction. Eyes are two full solar discs: white-hot centres with amber halos. In the post-game palette of true daylight colours, it reads as a creature from a different, brighter world — because it is.
signature_idea: First Dawn — summons a true solar field that replaces all weather effects, boosts every Solar- and Light-typed move by ×1.5 for five turns, and deals full-power physical Solar damage to the target with a follow-through Light pulse that hits every remaining opponent at half power; the move the game was building toward.
hook: The reward for completing the journey. The moment Dawnbrael steps into real sunlight for the first time, the game earns everything it promised.

name: Galesoar
concept: A sky-bound storm-predator discovered within the Wind-Eye sky-grotto — a perpetually swirling column of cloud with a hollow eye at the centre where this creature hunts. Built like a swift crossed with a barracuda, it exists at the exact intersection of storm and speed, riding updrafts as though gravity were an opinion. The Wind-Eye was formed by its roosting centuries ago; locals thought it was a weather phenomenon until the grotto was explored. It is not malicious — it simply makes storms as an incidental byproduct of moving fast.
visual: Streamlined spear-bird silhouette; the body is a compressed teardrop with swept-back wings almost invisible at speed. Feathers are slate-blue and cloud-white, tipped at the primaries with trailing static-arc lines in diamond-cyan. The beak is a blunt ram shape, crackled with ambient charge. Eyes are wide-spaced, calm, predatory. The 32px icon is all swooping line-weight.
signature_idea: Spear Gale — charges with extreme priority from a great height, dealing physical Storm damage that ignores Defense buffs; the first move to have true vertical arc in the battle animation.
hook: For players who love the fastest thing in the room — this one makes every other Storm-type feel slow.

name: Voltharrow
concept: Found at Thunderroost — a split-rock pillar on Windward Stair II where lightning strikes the same point every storm with uncanny precision because this creature wills it. Voltharrow is a storm-javelin kin, a narrow aerodynamic being that has evolved to be the most efficient conductor of electricity in Vesperholm. When lightning hits Thunderroost, it arcs directly through Voltharrow's body and re-emits as a column of light so bright it briefly brightens the constellations overhead. The locals regard Thunderroost as a sacred light-site; they have been inadvertently worshipping the kin inside it.
visual: Long and narrow as a thrown javelin — the body is a straight rod of deep storm-blue with sharp swept-back wing-fins. Down the length of the body run parallel conductor-grooves that glow blinding diamond-cyan when charged. The head is a blunt wedge, the tail a forked arrester. When fully charged, it pulses light in a rapid stutter — a storm-light strobe in a single body.
signature_idea: Conductor Burst — absorbs all Storm-type moves directed at it this turn and converts that energy into a massively amplified Light-type special blast on its next action; a glass cannon that rewards being hit.
hook: The niche collector's trophy: a javelin of living lightning that converts punishment into power.

name: Frosthollow
concept: Dwelling in Aurora Hollow — a sheltered ice-cave off Hushfrost Pass whose ceiling is permanently lit by a trapped aurora ribbon — Frosthollow is a great bear-like creature that has lived inside the aurora itself for so long that the light has become part of its biology. Its fur is frost-white but emits a continuous aurora sheen in greens and diamond-cyan. It is profoundly unhurried — it moves with the slow patience of someone who has watched the aurora cycle for centuries. The hollow it inhabits is warm despite the frost because its presence regulates temperature around itself as a side effect of carrying so much light.
visual: Large bear shape, wider and lower than tall; fur is snow-white with aurora banding visible through it — soft green and cyan underfur that glows without heat. The face is broad and calm, with deep ice-blue eyes. The paw-pads are transparent ice-crystal. When idle, slow aurora ribbons drift from its back like a cape that is also a sky. Silhouette reads gentle and immense.
signature_idea: Aurora Mantle — wraps itself in a living aurora that reflects half of all incoming Special damage back at the attacker while healing the user by a small amount each turn for three turns; the patient, glowing fortress.
hook: A bear made of polar light. The aurora-cape animation in battle will be the image players describe to friends who haven't played yet.

name: Heliovast
concept: Sealed inside the Helia Vault — a reliquary off Sunvault Climb whose door can only be unlocked by Sunsketch — Heliovast is the most concentrated pocket of stored sunlight in Vesperholm. It resembles a vast solar-ray fish, drifting through the sealed interior of the vault in a self-sustaining solar current. The vault was built specifically to contain it safely, because its presence causes nearby plants to bloom years ahead of schedule and dormant seeds from other regions to germinate in the stone cracks. It doesn't fight to harm — it radiates, and the radiation is overwhelming.
visual: A great disc-bodied ray with an enormous central solar-eye at the front face, surrounded by radiating fin-rays like a living sun diagram. The body is deep gold with white-hot veins. The fin-rays are translucent amber, trailing fading light halos at their tips. The eye is an intense white-core disc. Even at idle, the battle background behind it yellows. The silhouette at 64px is a sun — because it is one.
signature_idea: Solar Surge — charges for one turn building internal solar pressure, then releases a total-immolation Special strike that deals Solar damage to all opponents and leaves a persistent Sunfield that boosts Solar-type attacks for three turns.
hook: The one kin where catching it makes the battle screen itself change colour. Players will remember exactly where they first saw it.

name: Prismolith
concept: The singular inhabitant of Crystoll Vault — a deep late-game spur off Cinderhead Mine accessible only after Starreach is earned. The Vault is a geode chamber the size of a cathedral, and Prismolith is the crystal formation at its heart that was always also alive. It was misidentified as a mineral formation for decades by Cinderhead miners who gave it a number and a survey note. When the last constellation is relit, the Vault floods with starlight, and what everyone thought was a geological curiosity stands up. It moves like geology — extremely slowly, with enormous inevitability.
visual: A great quadrupedal form made entirely of faceted crystal — dark amethyst at the base, graduating through deep teal to diamond-cyan at the crown. No clear head; the leading face is a cluster of large hexagonal crystal lenses. The body refracts every available light source into a scatter of internal spectral patterns. At the right angle, its silhouette is a walking prism. Even at 32px it reads as something geometrically alien and beautiful.
signature_idea: Refraction Wall — bends all incoming Light-type attacks back at full power toward their origin, and converts 25% of incoming physical damage into flat HP recovery; the one kin for which being hit by Light feels like a mistake.
hook: The geological creature that is also a light sculpture. The design brief that will challenge and delight the pixel artist more than anything else in the game.

name: Zephyrvast
concept: A second Wind-Eye candidate — a colossal atmospheric jellyfish that drifts at the ceiling of the Wind-Eye sky-grotto. Where Galesoar is a predator of the storm, Zephyrvast is the storm itself given imprecise shape. Its body is a translucent bell of compressed storm-air; its trailing filaments are live lightning channels that it uses not for attack but for navigation, grounding itself briefly to the earth to take a bearing. Locals on Galehigh Terraces have called it the 'cloud-bell' for generations; no one suspected it was a kin until a kite-runner accidentally caught one of its filaments.
visual: Enormous bell-jellyfish of translucent storm-grey cloud-matter; the bell glows faintly diamond-cyan at the rim and darker storm-blue at the crown. Trailing filaments of forked lightning hang below, each ending in a grounding arc. At rest it pulses slowly like a breathing bell. At 64px it is an ominous dome filling the top half of the frame.
signature_idea: Charge Field — discharges all its filaments simultaneously, creating a persistent storm field that inflicts paralysis on any kin that uses a contact move for three turns; a beautiful trap that punishes physical attackers for touching it.
hook: The giant jellyfish made of weather. The creature that most makes players feel the Wind-Eye is a place with actual ecology.

name: Abyssmare
concept: The apex inhabitant of Tideglass Cavern — a micro-dungeon in the Dimglass Coast II cliff face where the sea has carved a cathedral of water-polished glass-stone through which deep tidal currents sing. Abyssmare is a colossal seahorse-leviathan that has lived so deep and so long that it has evolved bio-lanterns along its crest and flanks; when the cavern floods to the ceiling, it glows like a church. It is not aggressive — it is ancient and territorial in the way a reef is territorial, owning the space by simply being in it since before memory.
visual: Enormous seahorse body, six to seven times the height of a trainer; body is deep tide-blue with plated scales that catch light like tide-pools. Along the dorsal crest runs a chain of bioluminescent bio-lanterns in warm amber and cool diamond-cyan. The tail is a long, coiling anchor-rope of muscle. Eyes are wide, golden, and alien — seeing the player with the mild patience of a building. At 64px it barely fits the battle frame.
signature_idea: Tidecrusher — a slow, massively powerful physical strike that also lowers the target's Defense and douses all field weather effects; the inevitability of deep water.
hook: The Tideglass Cavern is where the game first shows players that the ocean has things in it they cannot imagine. Abyssmare is the proof.

name: Gallowstide
concept: A second Tideglass / Gullcry Rock candidate — the sea-bird apex of the Dimglass Coast. Gallowstide is a great storm-petrel grown to apex scale, a sea-bird so old and large it has learned to ride waterspouts as a kin rides Updraft Kite. At Gullcry Rock, the natural waterspout funnel at the cliff's end is Gallowstide's personal territory; mariners of Pearlmoor Quay leave fish offerings there before long voyages because legend says its screech can redirect a storm. It is not a gentle kin — it is the sea's indifference made fast and feathered.
visual: Enormous storm-petrel silhouette; wingspan several times its body length. Plumage is ocean-black on the upper surface and cold sea-foam white beneath. Wing-tips crackle with tide-static — the same blue-and-cyan arcing that occurs when wave breaks against lightning-charged rock. Eyes are golden-yellow, sharp, and perpetually searching. Every feather is sharply defined even at 32px because the contrast is absolute.
signature_idea: Gale Dive — stoops from maximum height on a single target, dealing high physical damage split between Tide and Storm types; the only move in the game that can trigger both STAB bonuses simultaneously if the user has both types.
hook: The seabird-predator players will immediately try to put in their party to see what it looks like in battle. It delivers.

name: Mycovast
concept: The apex kin of Spore Grotto — a vast, ancient fungal titan that has been growing through the rock of Glowmoss Deep for centuries, its mycelial network threading through both soil and stone until the two are indistinguishable in its body. The grotto it inhabits is as much part of it as its visible cap; remove the creature and the cave would slowly collapse. Mycovast communicates across its network in slow mineral resonance — a signal that takes hours but covers the whole eastern region. It is the oldest living thing in Vesperholm that isn't a star.
visual: An enormous mushroom-capped behemoth walking on six thick stone-threaded root-legs. The cap is deep earth-brown with bioluminescent Verdant spots in diamond-cyan and pale green. Beneath the cap hangs a fringe of glowing sporecurtain. The legs are stone-grey with thick mycelial cords wrapped around them like rope around pillars. The face is a flat, calm disc with two dim-glow eyes. At 64px it reads as a cave and a creature simultaneously.
signature_idea: Mycelial Surge — sends a pulse through its underground network that strikes every opponent with Verdant damage and inflicts the Rooted status (Speed halved, immune to forced switches) for two turns; the move that says the ground itself is the kin.
hook: The creature that makes players realise the whole grotto has been alive this whole time. A boss encounter with ecological horror charm.

name: Sporegrave
concept: A second Spore Grotto candidate — a great stone-tortoise whose shell has been colonised by a single enormous cap-fungus forming a symbiotic canopy so dense it is a small ecosystem. Sporegrave and Mycovast share the Grotto but occupy different ecological niches: where Mycovast is the network, Sporegrave is the patient wall — a creature that has not moved its core territory in so long that the Grotto's drip-stone formations have begun to grow around its shell's edges. It spore-breathes when threatened, filling the air with gentle calming spores that slow everything down.
visual: Low, extremely wide stone-tortoise; the shell is deep grey rock, crusted with cave-mineral formations at the front edges, and bears a vast domed mushroom-cap at the crown in ochre and pale gold. Underslung, broad face, deep-set amber eyes. Spore-vents along the shell rim emit slow particle wisps of pale green when agitated. Reads as a living geological feature.
signature_idea: Calming Spore — floods the field with sedative spore-mist, lowering both sides' Speed and halving all damage dealt for two turns; a sacrifice-field move that a Physical Wall uses to outlast anything.
hook: The tank for players who want to win by making the game slower until they're the last one standing.

name: Nullhusk
concept: The charged husk of the Hollowfen Stillworks — a derelict Hollowing null-works set-piece in Coldfog Marches. Once a thunderhead-kin captured and drained into a null-lantern to power the Stillworks machinery, Nullhusk has become something new: a storm-shaped void that still generates electricity through pure muscle memory while the light it once had has been entirely eaten. It haunts the Stillworks' shattered null-lantern array, discharging arcs of dead-charged dark-storm energy into the rusted machinery. It does not know it has been emptied — it keeps generating, a habit that outlasted its soul.
visual: A thunderhead-bull silhouette rendered in absolute void: the body outline is a deep storm-shape filled with dark non-light, negative-space body, but from it leak erratic arcs of dead-current in a sickly violet-grey that never quite reaches the warmth of true storm-blue. The eyes are empty null-lantern apertures — circular, glass-cold, unlit. The horns still crackle with charge. Reads as something that was majestic and is now entirely hollow.
signature_idea: Dead Circuit — discharges all accumulated null-charge in a single catastrophic arc that deals Dark damage scaled to how many status conditions are on the field, then wipes all field effects including its own; a scorched-earth move that clears everything.
hook: The most haunting optional encounter in the game: a thunderstorm that has been hollowed out. Players will feel Còr's philosophy as something terrible and real through this one battle.

name: Starvault
concept: The Starwell kin — encountered post-Crown in the Penumbra Ring's Starwell, a deep well of concentrated starlight that formed where all eight relit constellations' light intersects. Starvault is a near-legendary: a great armadillo-crab of pure crystallised starlight, its shell a vault of compressed light-memory. It has been absorbing the Skyweave's overflow for centuries, growing slowly into a living archive of every star-moment in Vesperholm's history. Finding it in the Starwell is one of the late game's quiet revelations: the place players assumed was just a plot location contains one last treasure.
visual: Low-slung, wide-bodied armadillo-crab hybrid; the shell is composed of faceted light-crystal plates in deep lunar-blue and bright diamond-cyan, each plate a lens that internally refracts a miniature star-cluster. Six crab-legs of polished bone-white crystal. The face is a broad stargazing shape with two enormous pale-gold eyes like captured stars. Small, perfectly composed, dense with detail — the 64px sprite will reward every zoom.
signature_idea: Vault of Stars — draws in all light-based effects on the field and stores them, then releases the full accumulated starlight in a single compounding special strike; the pay-off for patient field setup.
hook: The Starwell's secret: a creature that has been quietly collecting memories of every light ever restored. For players who finish the story, finding this feels like the world rewarding them for paying attention.

name: Lumenvast
concept: A second Starwell candidate — a vast geometric moth whose wings are stained-glass lattices of concentrated light. It drifts through the Starwell's depth in long, slow circuits, absorbing and radiating stored light in slow pulses. Where Starvault is a vault, Lumenvast is a prism — it does not collect light, it becomes light, and the transformation is always ongoing. In the Starwell's concentrated illumination, it is nearly painful to look at directly, but it circles the player's arrival with curious, watchful spirals rather than aggression.
visual: Enormous geometric moth — the wings are perfect pentagons composed of stained-glass-style leading in bone-white with filled panels of every light-spectrum colour. The body is long, narrow, covered in fine white-silk fuzz. At the centre of each wing, a diamond-cyan star-burst blazes through the glass. The eye-spots on the outer wings are true-star discs. At full wingspan it fills the battle frame.
signature_idea: Prismatic Convergence — focuses all available light into one point and releases it as a spectrum-wave that hits all opponents simultaneously for Light damage and randomly inflicts one status condition each based on the part of the spectrum that lands.
hook: A moth made of cathedral windows. Every child who ever pressed their face against stained glass will understand this creature immediately.

name: Saltmajor
concept: A deep-sea apex found in the Sunkbell Shallows off Saltreach Fen — a great nautilus-like creature whose shell is a labyrinthine fortress of calcium-and-salt layers built up over centuries of deep-brine exposure. It draws to itself the salt and mineral content of every water it enters, growing its shell incrementally with each passing year. The oldest nautili in the region have shells the size of boulders; Saltmajor is the oldest, so its shell has become an ecosystem shelter for dozens of smaller kin species that live among its whorls. It is essentially a living reef that also fights back.
visual: Enormous nautilus — the shell is a perfect spiral of layered deep-sea grey and salt-white, overgrown at the outer whorls with barnacle formations and anemone-like coral outgrowths in muted sea-greens and pale blues. The tentacle-crown that extends from the shell opening is wide and strong, tips each ending in a small bioluminescent node in diamond-cyan. The eyes are on wide stalks, deep amber, serene. The silhouette is an ancient spiral filled with life.
signature_idea: Salt Fortress — calcifies the exterior surface, raising Defense and Special Defense sharply for three turns and causing all physical attackers who strike it directly to take recoil damage from the sharpened shell-surface.
hook: The nautilus fortress. A kin that has been building its own armour for centuries and takes that personally when attacked.

name: Waveborne
concept: A second Tideglass Cavern candidate — a great wave-bear, a coastal apex predator adapted to riding the tidal surge through the Cavern's glass-stone corridors. Waveborne moves with the tide itself; when the Cavern floods and drains on its twelve-hour cycle, Waveborne rides each surge in a single arching dive from entrance to inner vault and back. Its fur is permanently saturated with brine, weighing it to enormous apparent mass; in the water it becomes the wave, in the air between tides it rests with massive, tide-exhausted calm.
visual: A massive bear of coastal build — wider than tall, with a low-slung, powerful swimmer's body. Fur is deep teal-blue saturated with seawater, hanging heavy. The face is blunt and intelligent, with tide-pool amber eyes. Along the shoulders and flanks, patches of barnacles and sea-glass have accumulated over centuries, forming natural armour. In the Cavern's diamond-cyan reflected light, the wet fur shimmers like moving water.
signature_idea: Tidal Surge — charges with the force of a collapsing wave, dealing massive physical Tide damage to the target and all kin adjacent to it, with a knockback that forces the target to switch out.
hook: The tide-bear that is the tide. For players who want the biggest, most immovable physical Tide attacker.

name: Stormvault
concept: A second Thunderroost candidate — a great cormorant-of-light that roosts at the same Thunderroost as Voltharrow but represents a different relationship with lightning. Where Voltharrow is the conductor, Stormvault is the capacitor: it absorbs each lightning strike and holds the charge in its feathers until it chooses to release it as pure light. Over centuries of lightning-charging, its plumage has become permanently luminous — it glows from within even on calm nights, which Windward Stair travellers have mistaken for a lighthouse. It has inadvertently saved ships and guided hikers as a side effect of hoarding light.
visual: Tall cormorant shape; the body is deep storm-blue-black with every feather outlined in a faint internal glow that collectively makes the bird luminous. Wings, when spread, reveal dense diamond-cyan light stored in the feather structure — like a bird-shaped stained-glass backlit from within. Eyes are wide, white-gold, calm. At 64px the feather-glow detail makes it read as both a predator and a lantern.
signature_idea: Stored Arc — spends one turn accumulating charge (boosting Special Attack sharply), then releases a combined Storm and Light special strike with doubled base power; the long-game sniper of storm-types.
hook: The lighthouse bird. Players who encounter it at Thunderroost will immediately understand why mariners thought it was a navigation aid.

name: Frostcarve
concept: A second Aurora Hollow candidate — a great ice-lynx carved from the same aurora-ice as the hollow walls, so perfectly camouflaged that early explorers of the hollow mapped it as a geological feature. Frostcarve is an ambush predator whose hunting strategy relies entirely on stillness and the aurora's interference with visibility; it can remain motionless for hours, its aurora-patterned coat matching the shifting light perfectly. Unlike Frosthollow's patient warmth, Frostcarve is cold patience with violent intent — the aurora's killing edge.
visual: Large lynx built for ice: powerful, broad-shouldered, low-to-ground, with massive cushioned paws for silent movement on ice. The coat is white with aurora banding — green-to-cyan shifting patterns that match the Hollow's ceiling light precisely. The ear-tufts are icicle-spires. The eyes are pale green and unnervingly still. In the hollow's light it is nearly impossible to spot; in open battle its coat shifts in slow aurora animation.
signature_idea: Aurora Ambush — can only be used from an invisible-phase (if Lunar Drift or equivalent has been used); deals triple physical damage and always causes the Frostbite status; the assassin move that rewards set-up.
hook: The ambush predator disguised as a light show. Players who camp in Aurora Hollow long enough to notice the 'rock formation' has eyes will get the most satisfying optional encounter in the north region.

name: Solavast
concept: A second Helia Vault candidate — a great solar-crab of Vesperholm's pre-dusk era, sealed in the Vault alongside Heliovast as a guardian-creature placed there by the original star-tenders. Where Heliovast is pure solar output, Solavast is solar persistence: it has conserved and rationed its stored sunlight across centuries, and each movement is careful and deliberate, as a creature that understands precisely how much energy it has left and does not intend to waste a ray of it. It is the last guardian of a way of life Vesperholm has forgotten.
visual: A vast crab — six legs plus two massive solar-collector claws angled like parabolic reflectors to catch and focus light. The shell is bone-white with solar-fire orange and gold inlay, cracked in places and showing the amber glow within. The eyes are on long stalks, solar-disc pupils with thin concentric rings. The collector-claws are always angled toward the light source. Reads as both ancient and functional — a piece of solar engineering that is also alive.
signature_idea: Solar Collect — passively stores incoming Solar and Light-type damage as charges; releases accumulated charges as a devastating flat-power physical solar claw-strike that grows stronger the more it has absorbed.
hook: The old guardian who outlasted his purpose and found a new one. Players who discover the Vault's second inhabitant will feel the world's history deepen around them.

name: Embergave
concept: A second Ember-type apex candidate for the south region — a great cave-bear that descended into the Tinderwick mines decades ago to hibernate near the forge-warmth and emerged subtly changed: its fur absorbs and re-radiates heat, and it has become the warmest single living thing in the south valleys. It does not breathe fire; it is fire, in the gentle sense — everything near it warms, things it brushes ignite slowly, and it leaves a faint scorch-path wherever it walks. Miners leave it respectful offerings because its wandering through the lower tunnels keeps the pipes from freezing.
visual: Massive bear built for caves: compact, low-slung, with a barrel chest and a broad, wedge-shaped head. The fur transitions from deep charcoal at the extremities to glowing ember-amber at the chest and belly, as though internally lit. Between the coat's guard hairs, faint heat-shimmer distortion is visible. The eyes are deep orange-red. Claws leave brief ember-trails on whatever they touch.
signature_idea: Forge Charge — a smashing physical blow that also sets the terrain to a Forge-Warmth field for three turns, boosting all Ember-type physical moves and inflicting passive Burn on any kin that uses direct contact moves.
hook: The mine-bear who became a furnace. South-region players who revisit the tunnels will find an apex that belongs to the world they already know.

name: Verdanthorn
concept: An apex verdant candidate for the Lowleaf Hollow deep canopy — a great mantis-like predator that has evolved in the deepest bio-luminescent forest where speed and camouflage are everything. Verdanthorn uses its bioluminescent patterns not for display but as a weapon: it can flash them in precise sequences that blind opponents momentarily, then strikes in the gap. In the Glowmoss Deep, it is both invisible and blinding in the same moment. It is the dark mirror of the forest's gentle glow — light as predation, not warmth.
visual: Tall bipedal mantis — long, thin body in deep forest-green with bioluminescent stripe-patterns in acid-green and diamond-cyan down the limbs and thorax. The forelimbs are long scythe-arms with glowing serrated inner edges. The head is a flattened triangular disc with compound eyes that can strobe independently. When attacking, the whole body flares in a rapid pattern — a living stroboscope.
signature_idea: Flashstrike — strobes its bioluminescent patterns to blind the target (guaranteed Confusion), then immediately follows with a critical-hit-guaranteed physical Verdant slash; a two-part move that plays as a single seamless animation.
hook: The forest's ambush predator. Players who love elegant glass-cannon design will find Verdanthorn's strobe-then-strike pattern the most satisfying execution in the east region.

name: Dustsovran
concept: An apex Stone candidate for the Cinderhead Mine's deepest galleries — a great armadillo-runner that has adapted to the Mine's narrow horizontal tunnels by becoming extremely fast over stone surfaces. It navigates by echolocation but also by reading stone-vibration through its belly-plates, making it impossible to ambush in its home environment. It moves by curling into a dense mineral sphere and rolling at extraordinary speed through tunnel curves — a living cannonball of compressed stone.
visual: A wide, low armadillo with an exaggerated barrel-roll build; the shell is dense faceted stone-grey with lighter quartz veins catching the Mine's lantern light. The unrolled form shows a blunt-nosed, alert face with deep-set mineral eyes of dark amber. When rolled, it is an almost-perfect sphere of grey-and-quartz that vibrates faintly with internal mechanism.
signature_idea: Stone Roll — curls to a sphere and launches across the field at extreme Speed, dealing Stone physical damage and lowering the target's Speed by two stages; ignores terrain-penalty effects.
hook: The Stone-type speedster. Players who assumed all rock kin were slow will catch this one and immediately rethink their party.

name: Rimfrost
concept: An apex Frost candidate for Hushfrost Pass — a serpent-of-cold that inhabits the ice-canyon walls of the Pass itself, emerging through the coldfog when temperatures drop to extremes. It is essentially a living blizzard compressed into serpent form: when it moves, the air around it drops sharply and the coldfog thickens. The Hollowing's coldfog and Rimfrost's natural freeze-field are difficult to distinguish from the outside, which has made the Pass especially dangerous — travellers with Emberward can push through Hollowing coldfog, but cannot push through Rimfrost's territory without facing it first.
visual: Long ice-serpent, wide-bodied and muscular with overlapping scale-plates of opaque frost-white and translucent ice-blue. The head is a wide flat triangle with a crest of ice-spike fins. The eyes are pale mint-green, barely visible through the frost-rime that builds on the face in cold air. When disturbed, it exhales coldfog that genuinely blurs the screen for a moment.
signature_idea: Deep Freeze Aura — as an entry ability rather than a move: on entry to battle, lowers all opponents' Speed by one stage and creates a Frost Field that persists for five turns, giving Frost-type moves priority and causing all contact moves to risk Frostbite.
hook: The weather serpent you didn't know was different from the weather. The pass encounter that makes players check their Emberward carefully before entering.

name: Embralux
concept: An apex Ember/Light candidate for the south region's secret Lumenary approach — a great phoenix-fox that embodies the moment between ember and starlight: the exact colour temperature where a flame is indistinguishable from a star. It inhabits the warm updraft columns around Tinderwick's lighthouse and has been spotted ascending and descending from the direction of the Ember constellation for generations. Some star-tenders believe it is a messenger between the anchor-kin and the constellation itself — the light-courier of the south sky.
visual: Sleek, long-limbed fox with enormous flame-and-star-ray tail plumes that trail behind it like a comet's tail. The body is amber-to-white radiant, as though lit from inside. The plume-tails shift between ember-orange at the base and cool diamond-cyan at the feathered tips — the gradient between fire and starlight. The ears are long and spark-tipped. The 64px sprite will look like a running star.
signature_idea: Ember Ascent — a rising strike that deals Ember damage on the way up and Light damage on the way down as the attack arc completes; triggers both STAB bonuses if the user holds both types, and always sets a Radiance field on landing.
hook: The fox that is also a comet. For players who fell in love with the south region's warmth and wanted an apex that belongs entirely to that feeling.
